### TAG-206: Runtime directive

**Status:** ⬜ Not started

## Software Notes

A sibling directive to `@domain`, something like `@runtime(consumable)` (bare digital logic staying the unmarked default, matching how `@domain` is already opt-in), checked the same way — a small, cheap addition given `assertNoTransformRuleSymbolCollidesWithPort`-style per-definition inspection is already the established pattern for this class of decision.

The need for this rose during our construction of [TAG-201](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-201/support-multi-operand-stoichiometry-and-multi-emission-fills-via) when we realized rule transformations need to be handled differently if we are using the shaking bag model of circulating tokens being consumed to activate transformation rules, as compared to discrete digital networks where tokens can flow to multiple destinations simultaneously, two very different modes of observation vs consumption.

The process of compiling VHDL for the two domains will be starkly different as well, so this directive is necessary for the developer to mark their code intentionally to have it be treated by either of the two pipeline paths - at some point the compiler will be able to detect the need for the consumable tokens but this is a first step in partitioning the problem for downstream development.

Necessary work to fulfill [TAG-203](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-203/parsing-pipeline)
